She decides to investigate these mysterious circumstances herself, where she comes upon these corrupted critters in the woods.
  • After figuring out what's going on with these creatures, you then "use and transform symbols to create paths through the creatures' insides.

Oh I do love an eldritch horror creature, I do, especially one that at first glance may only be slightly different from what I'm used to seeing. Eldritch Empathy, then, seems like a grand ole game to satisfy my wanton need to experience such things. It's a puzzle roguelite that isn't exactly a Papers Please-like but certainly feels reminiscent of one, where you have to "analyse corrupted creatures, purify their emotions and learn how to communicate with an eldritch being.".

You kick things off by embodying Eike, a "young woman who has strange dreams and sightings of twisted creatures in the woodlands neighbouring the sleepy Swiss village she lives in." She decides to investigate these mysterious circumstances herself, where she comes upon these corrupted critters in the woods. You need to thoroughly inspect them, using a book to determine what is going on with them and what they need exactly; it's akin to checking the passport rulebook in Papers Please, hence the comparison.

After figuring out what's going on with these creatures, you then "use and transform symbols to create paths through the creatures' insides. You may use care and precision to navigate to the correct corrupted emotion you have identified from your investigation and purify it. You may also use your tools to cause harm. Whatever you choose, your actions will have consequences." Ominous! You can also strategy your runs ahead of time, heading down paths that may offer you some boons here and there, like the option to restore a bit of sanity (it's one of those Lovecraftian kind of horror games, as loathe as I am that we still have to reference that guy).

Also be wary of the fact that actions you take out in the woods can affect your home and community. It's a roguelite with consequences! Mwahahha! Looks pretty neat overall, and has some tasty pixel art attached to it too. No release date just yet, but I'd assume it'll arrive no earlier than next year. You can wishlist it right here.

  • “With Wuling’s story wrapping up, and the main story taking us through all the heavy moments, we want to give you a change of pace with a lighthearted, upbeat upgrade,” mentioned Arknights: Endfield producer Light Zhong in a press release.
  • Here is an overview of the upgrade, via GRYPHLINE:.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Publisher GRYPHLINE and developer Mountain Contour will release the version update “Meeting You in the World o’Shrooms” for free-to-play 3D RPG Arknights: Endfield on November 25, the companies confirmed. The game’s latest live stream also introduced the upcoming version 2.0 update, which takes players to Gypsosia and aboard the Rhodes Island landship, and teased 10 characters who will join the journey across upcoming content updates.

“With Wuling’s story wrapping up, and the main story taking us through all the heavy moments, we want to give you a change of pace with a lighthearted, upbeat upgrade,” mentioned Arknights: Endfield producer Light Zhong in a press release.

Here is an overview of the upgrade, via GRYPHLINE:.

Version Update “Meeting You in the World o’Shrooms”.

Strange mushrooms have overrun an abandoned dam outside Wuling, where Landbreakers worship a giant mushroom and visitors keep slipping into hallucinations. There, the Endministrator meets Kay, a Rhodes Island Operator who has been adventuring alone across Talos-II in search of them. Kay happily shares everything she treasures, including a towering stack of honey waffles. But which would she choose: a mountain of waffles or a dear friend?

A Nature Vanguard with a carefree fighting style, Kay throws weapons that scatter across the battlefield, then gathers them up for a heavy hammer slam. Along the way, she drops Picnic Snacks that heal her teammates.

The Old Dam, the update’s new area, has grown into a fairytale-like mushroom kingdom. Players fire Kay’s honey waffles at mushrooms to open doors and spin fungal bridges, and must avoid Loquacious Shrooms that scramble their sense of direction. Mushroom foes like the Bolete Prince guard the dam, and a mushroom as tall as a mountain waits at its heart.

Recent findings suggest that the update’s music leans into its whimsical tone, with Ori composer Gareth Coker and ambient producer Owsey returning to score Kay’s honey waffle adventure. It caps a first year in which the soundtrack has followed the story, from the sweeping sci-fi orchestral sound of Valley IV to the choir-driven battle against Alleikhreos, Typhoeus’s JRPG-inspired winter journey and the modern electronic take on Eastern music in Si’s painted world.

Later in the patch, every player who logs in during the Workers’ Guards: Roll Call event will receive the Operator Mimino and her signature weapon, Star of Tomorrow, for free, with event missions offering extra copies to reach full Potential. Operators Gilberta and Rossi also return in successive reruns.

For factory builders, Exclusion Zone Rebuilding is a new permanent mode in which players supply materials across four phases to restore the North Wuling Exclusion Zone, using the new Forge of Luminance to transform products on their conveyor belts. For a lighter break, Lucky Carrot’s Games of Wonder adds two multiplayer card games, Witch’s Darkjack and Band Uprising, that players can enjoy with friends or through matchmaking.

A First Look at Version 2.0 and Rhodes Island.

In a recent development, the livestream also previewed the next chapter of Arknights: Endfield, arriving in the latest year. Exiles have rolled out attacks across the Civilization Band, and their real target is Rhodes Island. The Endministrator sets out with Perlica into Gypsosia, the Cretaceous Frontiers, where players will be able to board and explore Rhodes Island itself, a massive landship. A 10-character teaser offered a glimpse of companions for the journey, including Warfarin, appearing as the leader of Rhodes Island, and M3, who returns looking completely different.

In a recent development, the chapter’s first update will add four upcoming maps at once, including Rhodes Island. Main Mission Early Unlock: Gypsosia will let players who have completed the main mission Remediation Progress skip ahead to the new story while still earning all beginner-event rewards. New modes are also in development for future updates, including a management sim with the Golden Branch Tribe and the Shattered Protocol combat mode.

In a recent development, arknights: Endfield is now Steam Deck Verified, with default controller support and every feature available on Valve’s handheld. The update also brings Despot Weaponized, a latest high-difficulty challenge series in Umbral Monument; the return of RISE! MEGA ARENA!, a two-Operator arena event; and new seasons of the Echoes of War combat mode.

Arknights: Endfield is available now for PlayStation 5, PC via the official launcher, Steam, and Epic Games Store, iOS via App Store, and Android via Google Play.

Learn how to get a mask in GTA 6 to stay anonymous when committing a crime

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (614 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamesradar

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that if you want to be a better criminal in Leonida, you're going to need to learn how to get a mask in GTA 6.
  • Recent findings suggest that you can buy a mask in GTA 6 from any of the gun stores.
  • According to recent reports, to wear a mask in GTA 6, you need to make sure that it's with you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that if you want to be a better criminal in Leonida, you're going to need to learn how to get a mask in GTA 6. Despite Rockstar making appearance a key factor in the new Wanted system, the game isn't super clear on the steps you can take to hide your identity – particularly as you're progressing through Chapter 1 of the GTA 6 missions list. Thankfully, I'm here to help you understand how to get neckwear in GTA 6, how to equip masks, and how to change them for new ones.

Recent findings suggest that you can buy a mask in GTA 6 from any of the gun stores. Chuck's Tackle & Shot in Key Lento sells them (look at the central stand with the alligator head atop of it) from the beginning of the game, but you can head to any Ammu-Nation retailer to find more. Open up the GTA 6 Index, head into the weapons tab, and you'll be able to find all the relevant shops on your map. When you begin exploring Vice City and Vice Beach, you'll also find thrift stores that sell novelty masks, and high-end retailers which sell very fancy (and expensive) coverings that can be worn as well.

According to recent reports, to wear a mask in GTA 6, you need to make sure that it's with you. You can add neckwear items to your loadout by visiting the wardrobe in your residences. Scroll to the accessories tab and that's where you'll find the Masks option, which separates them by brand. If you want options while you're on the road, you can also store some in the trunk of your personal vehicle in GTA 6 by highlighting it and pressing Square/X.

Sources indicate that with a mask in your loadout, wearing it is as simple as holding L1/LB to open your loadout. Press R1/RB to scroll to the items menu, and then select Mask from the neckwear slot located at twelve-o'clock in the wheel. Press A to put it on, press A to remove it. Easy enough, and vital if you want to lose some of your Appearance Heat after robbing a store with CCTV equipment.

While hovering over the neckwear slot of your loadout, you can also press up and down to change the wear style of your mask in GTA 6. The first will see the mask conceal your face, which will draw panicked reactions from shop clerks, while the second will let you fashion the mask more appropriately.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Here's a quick bit of background: Rockstar's regional release schedule meant GTA 6 launched at midnight on 19th November everywhere, local time.
  • In fact, according to data analytics firm Ampere Analysis, the early demand was such that 1.5m Xbox users in the US and 600,000 UK Xbox players briefly went Kiwi for the occasion of GTA 6's launch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that we already knew there'd be a frantic clamour for GTA 6 this week, and we also knew plenty of players would be eyeing up Xbox's 'New Zealand trick' to get in on the action early. But it's now being reported that a whopping 2m UK and US players took advantage of the trick - which, for context, equals more than a third of New Zealand's actual population.

Here's a quick bit of background: Rockstar's regional release schedule meant GTA 6 launched at midnight on 19th November everywhere, local time. As such, New Zealand was the first country in the world to see the hugely anticipated game go live, thanks to timezones. And because Xbox players can make purchases on any regional store easily, simply by changing their console's country, understandably impatient sorts opted to become temporary virtual New Zealand residents in their droves (on PlayStation, the process requires a regional account and payment in local currency so is more finicky).

In fact, according to data analytics firm Ampere Analysis, the early demand was such that 1.5m Xbox users in the US and 600,000 UK Xbox players briefly went Kiwi for the occasion of GTA 6's launch. Other countries highlighted by Ampere include Canada, where 200,000 Xbox players took the New Zealand plunge, Brazil (200,000 players), and Mexico (100,000 players).

By contrast, just 100,000 PlayStation players in the US opted to dive in early, reflecting, as Ampere notes, "the ease of being able to switch country in the account settings on Xbox consoles." And here's all that info in graph form:.

According to recent reports, amusingly, Newly introduced Zealand's tourist board tipped a wink to the sudden influx of virtual 'visitors', telling them "We'd love to have you". It also cheekily offered a video of cheerful tourists admiring the country's resplendent natural beauty "Life," read the accompanying caption, "because we're getting GTA 6 first.".

According to recent reports, some hours later and the rest of the world can now finally, officially join in the GTA 6 fun, and it's a game worth playing. Eurogamer's Chris Tapsell called it an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in his five star GTA 6 review. And if you need some help getting through the game now it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

Recent findings suggest that kelly Clarkson's feud with the Art of Play store became one of the strangest stories of 2026, as who would've thought a story about a pop star trying to buy an animatronic bird would draw so much attention? While the beloved Clarkson might've taken some hits in the court of public opinion, it sounds like the artist on the other side of the drama saw a substantial boost in patronage.

Bliss Kolb, the artist responsible for the $15,000 bird that was eventually purchased by another celebrity, is getting a ton of orders after this brouhaha. The Wall Street Journal reported that he's seen over 100 requests for his work, and that he's trying to wind down the orders. With that said, he's happy for all the attention he received and mentioned Clarkson in his comment:.

I've wanted for people to know about my work for decades. I appreciate that she liked it. This is happening at a time that I'm trying to wind down commitments.

The 70-year-old artist who lives in Seattle isn't trying to ramp up the amount he's doing these days, but he is grateful for the spotlight on the work he's made throughout his life. Out of all the hatred that came from this drama, I'm happy to hear some positivity came out of it, too.

‘I Know This Sounds Dark.’ The Advice Kelly Clarkson Gives Contestants When The Voice Goes Live.

It has been revealed that for those needing a refresher, this all started when Kelly Clarkson wandered into a Brooklyn store and inquired about the price of an animatronic bird on the wall. There's a discrepancy about what happened afterward, but the pop star went online and alleged that a worker at the store implied she couldn't afford the asking price, apparently not knowing who she was.

Recent findings suggest that the store, Art Of Play, told a different story. It was alleged that Clarkson was merely told the piece was one of a kind and not for sale. It became a substantial case of "he remarked, she said," with people reviewing security camera footage and drawing their own conclusions about it. There was also the random reveal that the owner of the store is an acclaimed children's author, but that didn't really have anything to do with the story.

Recent findings suggest that kelly Clarkson has had a wild year, but there have been some upsides on the back half of 2026 for her. The Kelly Clarkson Show received some substantial honors following its end, and she seems to be largely at peace with leaving the daytime talk show circuit.

In a recent development, who knows what's next for her as the holidays approach, but I can assume her kids won't be getting an expensive toy bird under the Christmas tree. However, based on the number of requests this artist is getting, it seems like it's perfectly possible that lots of folks would like to do something like that with his work.

Virginia Feito on the Film Adaptation of Her Novel ‘Victorian Psycho’

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2121 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The writer is the lowest form of life on a movie.- Martin McDonagh.
  • Recent findings suggest that when I finished editing my second novel, Victorian Psycho, I could not imagine we would be shooting the film adaptation the following year, mere months after the book’s publication.
  • I decided then to undertake this journey that would take me metaphorically to Hollywood but geographically to a county just outside of Dublin, where we would recreate the Ensor House of my novel.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The writer is the lowest form of life on a movie.- Martin McDonagh.

Recent findings suggest that when I finished editing my second novel, Victorian Psycho, I could not imagine we would be shooting the film adaptation the following year, mere months after the book’s publication. Generally, making a movie is one significant miracle produced by an amalgamation of thousands of other tiny miracles. But when I met Zach Wigon, I understood that this was a joyfully tenacious person who was going to make this movie if it cost him his life.

I decided then to undertake this journey that would take me metaphorically to Hollywood but geographically to a county just outside of Dublin, where we would recreate the Ensor House of my novel. Among film stars, an Irish crew, and (rumored) ticks, the adaptation of Victorian Psycho—based on my screenplay, which is based on my novel, which is based on my ego, I guess—was born. Throughout the shoot I kept a sort of pseudo diary in order to remember every surreal detail from which I still haven’t recovered. I’ve chosen to reproduce some of it here.

Director Zach Wigon and producer Lisa Kelly call me from the set on the first day of shooting (Zach and I have agreed I won’t visit the set until after the first week so the cast and crew can acclimate without me hovering over them, because I am an intense fame whore, and also, I suppose, to signal I’m not important enough to pull a P.L. Travers and attempt to boycott the movie).

Over the phone, the producer says she can’t wait to meet in person. I tell her I’m underwhelming.

Industry observers note that they promise to send me the dailies. I spend all day waiting for the dailies. The dailies never come.

Sources indicate that at around 9 p.m., I spiral because I don’t know whether to celebrate with Champagne or KFC. I decide to have both.

I finally get the dailies. I fall in love with Maika Monroe’s character so hard it’s like I have an obsessive crush circa 2006 whose Facebook photos I’m compulsively looking at. But in this case it’s the same scene throughout five almost identical takes of Maika calling a 10-year-old boy a little idiot.

Recent findings suggest that over the phone, Zach mentions concerns about a specific scene because we don’t have the budget for that many extras. I get carried away and suggest shipping over a whole battalion of free extras from Spain because, in my head, it’s going to be me and my friends, drunk and decked out in period clothing like we’re at a cheesy bachelorette party. One friend starts making childcare arrangements and another cancels her Holter monitor appointment so she can come to the shoot. What could go wrong?

I start to realize what could go wrong.

Recent findings suggest that I am informed we are probably no longer going to need the extras, and I feel a huge wave of relief as I uninvite my excited friends. I pack a suitcase for Ireland. It weighs 57 pounds.

I have a steak on the plane to Dublin at, like, 3 p.m., because when you’re flying business and somebody offers you steak, you take it.

The hotel room is wonderful, but I jokingly tell Zach over the phone that it’s on a first floor, so someone might crawl up and break in through the window and rape me, and he laughs at first but then is concerned and tells me to request a room on a higher floor, and I tell him it was a joke, but it wasn’t really.

I fill up the hotel room bathtub and call reception for a glass of red wine because I am a queen and I am queening. The glass doesn’t come, so in my anxious impatience I attempt to open a bottle of red wine sitting above the minibar. The cork crumbles because I’ve never understood how to use a corkscrew—like the compass in math class, I just faked my way through it my entire life and hoped for the best. So I call reception for another glass of red wine. They bring me all the glasses of wine and also properly uncork the bottle, and I watch Seinfeld in the bathtub while I drink red wine. I get drunk and paint my nails.

It has been revealed that I arrive on set slightly Bromazepamed. It is extremely surreal to exist in a set labeled “Mr. Pounds’s Bedroom.” I am used to living in the fictional world inside my head but not used to it becoming more real than real life itself.

It has been revealed that maika hugs me when we meet, and I swallow a sob and refrain from smelling her hair (partly because it is, in fact, a wig). Everyone on set appears so happy to meet me, I suspect a Good Bye, Lenin! situation in which I have been diagnosed with cancer and for some reason the cast and crew all know but I don’t know. This isn’t the plot of Good Bye, Lenin!, but you’ll know what I mean if you’ve seen it.

Zach asks me to read the VOs in every scene, which means I’m in the scene with Ruth Wilson, Jason Isaacs, and Maika, and I’m about to have a stroke.

Jason eats for real in every single take and has already gulped down seven sausage rolls, so if I fuck up my VO, I will kill myself.

It has been revealed that suddenly experiencing fiction collectively feels very superior to experiencing it privately. This does not bode well for the rest of my career as a novelist.

Industry observers note that there is a scene in a cramped drawing room in which I must read the VO, but I’m supposed to hide from the camera, so I crawl on all fours behind an antique couch and grovel my way around the room while the boom op steps on my hands. I secretly think the boom op hates me because I’m always in his way and have an irritating habit of apologizing when he slams into me.

I start developing Irish inflections, so I say it, “I start developing Irish inflections,” but the Irish seem happy about it, so I pursue it.

Jason Isaacs starts doing card tricks between takes because Jason Isaacs is actually magic and also indefatigable. Only one thing could ever defeat Jason Isaacs, and it’s the ghost allegedly living on the third floor.

In a recent development, even though Zach asked me to oversee the second unit, I don’t think anyone believes I’m actually going to do this—and between you and me, I don’t really even know what a second unit is. It doesn’t help I can’t concentrate on what we’re shooting because we’re in the middle of the woods and someone mentioned there were ticks, so I’m wrapping Sellotape around my ankles, hoping this way they won’t be able to crawl up my legs.

Recent findings suggest that like your worst trauma, I insert myself into the movie forever via a small cameo. I literally just have to stand in a wig while I smile and nod, but I do it in such a way that I ruin every single take. “Just smile…like a normal person,” the second-unit director says. I reason Zach can just cut me out of the movie, and I will only have wasted everybody’s time and money. There are worse things, like smiling normally but having no cameo. I cope by chewing on another Bromazepam and another chocolate bar. (Every morning I take the chocolate bar from the hotel minibar. It will invariably become an asset in the long afternoons on set, kind of like in prison or high school.).

Recent findings suggest that I change hotel rooms because I have developed an intense FOMO with which I’m always fearing there is a better hotel room for the same price somewhere in the vicinity. This FOMO is also rampant on set between the different units—in the first unit, you have the cinematographer, Nico Aguilar, laughing in the sunlight, talking about color palettes, while in the second unit, we’re shooting clocks and screaming at each other because we still have 17 establishing shots to go.

Anyway, I change hotel rooms, and the new room is so superior to my previous room it’s like an entirely new hotel. I consider changing hotel rooms further. Perhaps I can somehow upgrade my way into a presidential suite.

My parents visit the set. My dad peers over his glasses at the fake lobster cake, and when I tell him the toilets are in trailers, he sighs gravely.

It has been revealed that jason Isaacs convinces my dad to take up tennis again even though my dad’s not supposed to play tennis after his seven hernias. But my dad is so inspired by this actor, who is not a doctor but whose performance in The Patriot my dad can’t help but praise at least once a month, that he will immediately start playing tennis again upon his return to Spain, and whatever medical problems arise henceforth shall all be Jason Isaacs’s fault.

At the Shelbourne restaurant that night, my mom tells the sommelier how she can’t drink red wine anymore because it makes her anxious, and he kneels on the floor beside her and places a hand on his heart as if she were confiding something intimate to him like her fear of death.

Suddenly, real life feels less real than fictional life.

It has been revealed that obama is visiting Dublin and he’s booked the entire floor, so he essentially kicks me out of the Shelbourne (probably to stay in the JFK Suite next door to my room, which is disappointingly predictable), so I go to The Hoxton, because what is life if you’re not constantly changing hotel rooms? The Hoxton is really lovely, but I get OCD about the light bulbs in the room because they appear mismatched, so I ask housekeeping to change them, but they claim not to have any extra light bulbs, which sounds suspect—like, what do they do if a light bulb suddenly goes out? Do they just never replace it?

We end the shoot at 5 a.m. I am wearing a thick puffer coat and a thermal T-shirt and a furry hat, plus fur-lined boots over my Sellotaped ankles, although I wonder, If ticks can survive this temperature, they kind of deserve to live off my blood. Nobody else seems as concerned about the cold as me, but then again, most of them are Irish.

Recent findings suggest that sadly, when we wrap, we are all so exhausted everyone races to clean up and leave, and it is sort of anticlimactic. I don’t know what I was expecting, but balloons falling from the skies did flash through my mind.

It has been revealed that in the car on the way to our respective quarters, Zach and I look out the window, wide-eyed, like kidnapped children. Zach starts discussing a new project for us. I wonder if he is a sociopath.

Industry observers note that I type this over a year later, sitting at my desk in Madrid, striving to work on my next novel. I feel empty inside knowing there is no car to pick me up and take me to set and thereby escape reality for extended periods of time, until set becomes reality and reality becomes a limbo in which you wait for said reality.

Sources indicate that I am working on a novel, but also on four newly introduced scripts. I hope to return to reality someday.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ubisoft has confirmed more layoffs as part of its previously unveiled operational "reset", this time affecting 166 employees at its major Montréal and Québec City studios - the teams responsible for game series including Assassin's Creed and Far Cry.
  • GamesIndustry.biz reports the cuts - believed to equate to around four percent of the studios' total headcount - will impact employees working on projects either recently cancelled or significantly changed.
  • The publication also understands the cuts, stated to primarily impact production and support roles at Ubisoft Montréal and Québec City, include members of Vantage Studios - Ubisoft and Tencent's joint development venture announced last October, which focuses on the publisher's biggest franchises, including Far Cry, Rainbow Six Siege, and Assassin's Creed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ubisoft has confirmed more layoffs as part of its previously unveiled operational "reset", this time affecting 166 employees at its major Montréal and Québec City studios - the teams responsible for game series including Assassin's Creed and Far Cry. It indicates the cuts are necessary "to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs.".

GamesIndustry.biz reports the cuts - believed to equate to around four percent of the studios' total headcount - will impact employees working on projects either recently cancelled or significantly changed.

The publication also understands the cuts, stated to primarily impact production and support roles at Ubisoft Montréal and Québec City, include members of Vantage Studios - Ubisoft and Tencent's joint development venture announced last October, which focuses on the publisher's biggest franchises, including Far Cry, Rainbow Six Siege, and Assassin's Creed.

In a statement provided to Eurogamer, Ubisoft confirmed it is, "reducing its workforce by 166 positions across its Montréal and Québec City operations", adding: "As our portfolio evolves, our production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs.

"We deeply value the contributions of these teams and recognise the impact this may have on our colleagues," the statement continued. "We are committed to supporting them through this process with care and respect. Those affected are being provided with severance, extended health care benefits, career transition services and other resources.".

These latest job cuts are part of a "major organisational, operational and portfolio reset" revealed by Ubisoft in January. That initial announcement was accompanied by the news of two studio closures - affecting its Halifax mobile and Stockholm teams - plus the cancellation of six projects, including the much-delayed Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time remake.

Industry observers note that since then, 105 jobs have been cut at Red Storm Entertainment, the Ubisoft studio behind the Ghost Recon series, and around 380 employees were reportedly laid off when the publisher's Winnipeg and Belgrade teams shut in June. In October, Ubisoft closed Trials developer RedLynx and downsized its Singapore Assassin's Creed: Black Flag Resynced team, impacting a total of approximately 120 employees. Amid all this, Ubisoft developers have been on strike in response to the publisher's sweeping layoffs.

You'll be able to start looking for GTA 6 Transgressor locations after you complete the Thrillbillies mission in Chapter 2 and collect the Vapid Dominator from Wyman (if you have the Ultimate Edition, that is).

Sources indicate that he'll text to ask for help finding old wrecked Transgressors he can use to restore the classic car, which you'll then get to drive. There are three of these junks located around Port Gellhorn which you'll have to scan with the Waink It app.

The first wrecked Transgressor you can find is in a trailer park north of Sarena's Bargain Store in the middle of Port Gellhorn (you might have to zoom in to see the store). Head north, cross the road, and jump over the wall to find it there.

In a recent development, the second wrecked Transgressor is further north in the garage of the house opposite the Kolt & Associate's Stash House robbery (there's a metal sunflower standing in the garden, which makes it easier to recognise.) It's also to the east of Brook's Boatworks and the west of Wasteland Offroad. Head around the side of the house via the driveway to find the car in an open garage at the back.

Recent findings suggest that this last one is nice and easy, behind the Dirt Merchants mod shop in the south of Port Gellhorn. Simply head right via the track that leads behind the shop, following the fence on your right and then turn left to find the wreck at the back behind the kind of trailer park area.

In a recent development, once you have all three cars scanned, Wyman will take a little time to assemble it, and then call you asking to Buck him some money. Open the app, select the payment requests option, and then pay him the $1,500 for the car. This will give you a quest marker to collect it from his scrapyard.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 has only been out for a matter of hours, and players have already tracked down a UFO in the woods and a Bigfoot in the swamps.

Recent findings suggest that the UFO encounter is a random night-time event in Kelly County, on a dirt road near the Starlet Motel safehouse east of Port Gellhorn. You'll need to have finished the game's first chapter, and it's most reliable after 2am in-game.

As word spread late yesterday (18th November), it seems the event will kick off if you find a car at the side of the road with its headlights flickering, its trunk open, and clothes strewn around it. Follow the trail into the trees towards a blue glow, and you'll catch a UFO beaming down on a woman before it drops her and flies off. Head back to her car, as she requests, and the UFO returns for you. You apparently black out and come round three days later, and a bronze trophy called The Truth Is Out There should unlock.

You can seemingly trigger the event as either Jason or Lucia, and it isn't needed for 100 percent completion.

It has been revealed that and that's not the only close encounter you can expect, either. YouTuber Lazarbeam bumped into Bigfoot on the afternoon of 18th November, hours before the game launched in the UK, while one Reddit user reported that they weren't quite sure what they'd stumbled on, titling their post "I think I found Bigfoot".

Leonida's version of Bigfoot is actually the Skunk Ape, Florida's own swamp cryptid, and it can be found in the swamplands near Cottonmouth Lake in Mariana County as soon as free roam opens up. Listen out for a loud roar, then use Jason's tracking ability to follow it through the swamp. You may find it feeding on a deer carcass, while a second sighting has been reported south of Watson Bay.

It has been revealed that either way, the trail seemingly ends at a strange, human-like tree. Investigate it, and Jason blacks out, triggering a short cutscene in which the creature creeps up on him, as shown in this video. He later wakes near his vehicle, drenched in sweat. Save your ammo, though, as shooting at it won't do you any good.

Cryptids and aliens are, of course, something of a Rockstar tradition by this point. GTA 5's Mount Chiliad mystery kept players hunting for years, and Output Lag has already spotted two NPCs in a GTA 6 bar talking about goings-on there. Nobody has cracked a full Chiliad-style puzzle in the upcoming game yet, but I'm sure that's just a matter of when, not if.

It has been revealed that GTA 6 released today on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, although some have been getting in on the action earlier as a whopping 2m Xbox players in the UK and US took advantage of the trick of changing their console's country. Even New Zealand's tourist board tipped a wink to the sudden influx of virtual 'visitors', telling them "We'd love to have you". It also cheekily offered a video of cheerful tourists admiring the country's resplendent natural beauty. "Life," read the accompanying caption, "because we're getting GTA 6 first.".

Recent findings suggest that eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. And if you need some help getting through the game now it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

Multiple GamesRadar+ writers have gone through both options, and it's a lot less crucial of a decision in GTA 6 than you think, so here's what we know about the significance of shaking Mattia's hand.

Be aware of some very mild spoilers for later missions in Chapter 1 below.

Sources indicate that shaking Mattia's hand in GTA 6 makes no difference to any events in the Day Release mission. If you shake his hand, you shake his hand, and if you don't, you don't. Mattia doesn't even acknowledge that you left him hanging.

Sources indicate that later in the mission, Mattia offers Jason and Lucia some drugs in a nightclub and, again, accepting or refusing has no clear repercussions. Comparing videos of the choices side-by-side, there were no obvious differences between either outcome as the same thing happens regardless - Mattia either takes the drugs back or hands them over, stands up and leaves, then Jason and Lucia take to the dancefloor. The rest of the mission then plays out as normal.

As far as I can tell, turning Mattia down in either of these situations in Day Release has no long-term impact either as the "job" that he mentions at the end of the mission is critical to the story and can't be avoided. Just make sure you've done everything before the GTA 6 Tourist Trap mission as it's an important one – and if you get stuck, my GTA 6 Tourist Trap walkthrough can help.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that updates are generally good for your devices. The latest Chrome upgrade, for example, patches an actively exploited security vulnerability, while Apple's latest updates stop people from seeing iMessages they shouldn't have access to. In most cases, it's beneficial to update your tech to the latest software version whenever possible.

Recent findings suggest that sadly, updates aren't all perfect, as Google Pixel users are discovering this week. As reported by Android Authority, Google's November update apparently shipped with a bug that breaks some Pixel 10 and Pixel 11 cameras. Seeing as Pixels are rather famous for their shooters, this is a decidedly unfortunate glitch.

Here's the situation: Following the November update, some users are opening their Pixel Camera apps to find an error that reads, "Something went wrong. Close and open the Camera app again," with a "Learn More" link to, well, learn more. Others aren't receiving the error, but are instead running into a blank Camera viewfinder, as if the lens is totally covered. What's more, some users are reportedly saying that the matter is present on third-party camera apps, not just the Pixel Camera app. That would imply this is an issue with the camera system-wide, not just the Pixel Camera app itself.

Recent findings suggest that to be clear, it doesn't seem like this is a universal issue. It's not like all Pixel users are now running with broken cameras. But based on the forum complaints Android Authority discovered, it seems reasonable to assume that this glitch isn't limited to just a handful of unlucky Pixel owners.

Luckily, there is an apparent workaround here, though it's not totally obvious. Some owners are having no luck restarting their Pixels, while others report that a factory reset wasn't enough to restore camera functionality.

According to recent reports, what does appear to work, however, is shutting your Pixel down and waiting five minutes or so. It's not clear why, but giving your Pixel a chance to "breathe" seems to shake the glitch and bring back your camera. As Android Authority reports, that fix comes from "Diamond and Gold product experts" on Google's Support forum.

According to recent reports, if your Pixel's camera is giving you grief following the November enhancement, this workaround is definitely worth a try—especially since more drastic measures don't actually seem to do anything. As the glitch does seem to be rather widespread, I wouldn't be surprised to see Google issue a patch in the coming days. But until then, turning your phone off for five minutes may be a decent compromise.

Industry News: A Survivor of Alleged Sex Abuse at Miss Hall’s School in the Berkshires Speaks Out.

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2735 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • At 6:04 on the morning of March 29, 2024, my phone lit up with a long text from Matt Rutledge.
  • It has been revealed that I was thirty-seven years old.
  • It has been revealed that he had spent years teaching me to use his word for it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

At 6:04 on the morning of March 29, 2024, my phone lit up with a long text from Matt Rutledge. The head of school had called him the night before, he wrote, while he was watching television with his wife. He was on paid administrative leave, his school email was frozen, and he assumed this was about him and me. He called what he had done to me a relationship. He didn’t regret his feelings for me. Could I call him when his wife was out of the house?

It has been revealed that I was thirty-seven years old. I was a few weeks out from my partnership interview at a New York law firm. I had a husband and a three-year-old son. I spend my working life telling clients which sentences will look bad in discovery. I read that text twice, and my first thought was, How can I help him?

It has been revealed that he had spent years teaching me to use his word for it. It was never a relationship. He groomed me, he exploited me, and he raped me.

Vanity Fair has written about that morning before. Evgenia Peretz opened “Girls, Interrupted” with that text in January 2025, and she went back to Miss Hall’s last fall after the investigation came out. In March, Dan Adler covered the indictment. This time I’m telling it myself.

Later that morning an email arrived from an attorney in Boston. Subject line: “Reaching out about Miss Hall’s School.” I didn’t open it right away. I didn’t need to. Some part of me had been composing that email in my head since I was a teenager. The attorney represented a woman named Melissa Fares, a Miss Hall’s alumna who had been there a few years after me. I had never heard her name.

She had heard mine. Years earlier, older girls at the school had told her about me. She held on to my name, and when she went to a lawyer she remembered it. By then I had married and changed it, and they found me anyway.

Recent findings suggest that I called Matt and asked. “Who is Melissa?” There was a pause long enough to hear him decide something, then a sigh, and then he told me he had had sex with Melissa while she was a student.

Here is what I did next, and I’d ask you to withhold judgment. I told him I would call the lawyer, find out what she had, and report back.

Industry observers note that that’s what twenty-two years of being groomed looks like at a desk in Midtown. You don’t make a decision. The decision was made for you a long time ago, in a dorm room, and you’re simply carrying it out.

Recent findings suggest that I did call the lawyer. And when I heard my own voice say “I’m not ready to talk to you, I want to talk to Melissa,” I think that was the first sentence in two decades that I said entirely for myself.

It has been revealed that melissa called that afternoon. I don’t remember how she started. I remember what I said before she got far.

“I’ve been waiting for your call for twenty years.”.

Recent findings suggest that I meant it literally. Some part of me had always known I wasn’t the only one. I just couldn’t go looking. I could only wait to be found.

Hilary Simon and Melissa Fares, photographed in Far Rockaway, Upcoming York, 2025.

In a recent development, she told me her story, and I heard my own memories come out of a stranger’s mouth. He called her “Little One.” He called me “Little One.” He took her to the same hotel in Northampton. He told her he would kill himself if she ever told anyone, which is a thing he had also told me, more than once, in nearly the same words. He had made himself the center of her emotional world before he ever touched her. He had a script.

For twenty years he had me believing that what happened was singular, and that it was my fault. By the end of that call it was a pattern, and I was a data point. I was not special. It is a strange thing to grieve, not being special to the person who hurt you. I grieved it anyway.

After more than three decades teaching at that school, he resigned the same day.

Industry observers note that I arrived at Miss Hall’s, an all-girls boarding school in Pittsfield, Massachusetts, in the fall of 2001. I was fourteen, homesick, and like every other girl my age, positive I was more grown up than I was.

Rutledge had been teaching history there for a decade. He was a big man with a booming voice, married with two daughters. He lived with his family in a school-owned house across the street from the main entrance. He used to cut the lunch line announcing himself as “Mr. Wonderful.” Girls talked about him like he was a minor deity. They also mentioned, in the breezy way teenagers mention terrible things, that he had a type.

It has been revealed that some evenings, he was one of the adults who did bed checks in the dorms. The others always stood in the doorway. He came in and sat on the edge of my bed.

By the next fall he was my advisor and my cross-country coach. There was no door at that school he couldn’t open. On the long drives to meets, he told me to sit next to him in the school van. He called me his copilot. The rest of the team sat behind us. He would put his hand on my upper thigh, or pull me close until our legs were touching. I watched the Berkshire hills go by and tried not to look down.

That was the first line he crossed. I was fifteen. After that he crossed them one at a time until there were none left. He kept abusing me for years after I graduated.

From the outside, those years looked like a success story.

I went to college and then law school. I became a civil defense attorney. I got married. I had a son. I was good at my job.

In a recent development, I could find the unanswered email in ten thousand pages of discovery. The report nobody followed up on. I couldn’t open my own file.

When I tell this story, people ask me some version of the same question. How did nobody notice?

In the late 1990s, years before I ever set foot on Miss Hall’s campus, a student stood up at a school meeting and said Mr. Rutledge was having sex with another student. The school suspended her for the rest of the year, barred her from graduation and made her write him an apology letter. He kept teaching.

According to recent reports, on my graduation day, Rutledge kissed me and told me that he loved me. A classmate told a staff member, who reported it to the administration. In a memo, Rutledge admitted telling me he loved me but said “[it was] not a romantic expression.” He denied the kiss. They took his word for it. No one called me or my parents.

Hilary Simon on graduation day.

A few years later, after a family reported that he had made advances toward their daughter, the head of school at that time, Jeannie Norris, put a warning to Rutledge in writing. “This isn’t the 70s or the 80s,” she wrote. “Society has no stomach for any kind of inappropriate behavior between adults and girls or teachers and students.” She was worried about the school’s reputation, and about his. In the letter she mentioned the incident had “the potential for seriously damaging the School and your [Rutledge’s] reputation.” He was not fired.

In a recent development, over the years that followed Rutledge was made chair of the history department and collected faculty honors. More than one person gave the school my name as a girl he had singled out. Nobody ever called me. In June 2023, I heard another alumna tried to raise concerns about him with the head of school at that time. He was still teaching nine months later, when Melissa reported him.

In a recent development, in August 2025 Miss Hall’s published the results of an outside investigation it had commissioned from Aleta Law. The investigators substantiated grooming and abuse by Rutledge involving at least five students. They found school leadership had been warned about him over the years and hadn’t acted. Staff members told investigators they had suspected him and kept quiet, some because they feared retaliation, others because they assumed no one in charge would listen.

It went beyond Rutledge. The investigation found that seven other Miss Hall’s employees had engaged in sexual misconduct with students, dating back to the 1940s. Eight adults across eighty plus years. That’s a culture of abuse.

According to recent reports, A Berkshire County grand jury has since indicted Norris on a charge of reckless endangerment of a child. She has pleaded not guilty. Another former Miss Hall’s teacher has been indicted for assault with intent to rape and indecent assault and two counts battery of a student. He has also pleaded not guilty.

Sources indicate that I read all sixty pages of the Aleta Law report in one sitting. Nothing in it surprised me. It still knocked the air out of me to see my adolescence reduced to numbered findings.

Melissa arrived at Miss Hall’s in 2007, two years after I left.

People sometimes call us friends. That’s true, but it’s a small word for it. I call her my sister survivor.

Industry observers note that I wouldn’t be writing this if Melissa hadn’t gone first. She went to the school alone. In April 2024, she told her story publicly. A few weeks later, I told mine. Then other women came forward. They remarked Rutledge had abused them too.

In October 2024, the Berkshire district attorney said he didn’t believe he could charge Rutledge. In Massachusetts, the age of consent is sixteen. Under the law, a teacher could claim that a sixteen- or seventeen-year-old student had consented.

Melissa and I set out to change the law. We testified at the State House and knocked on every door that would open. Enough Abuse, a Massachusetts nonprofit, had been fighting for this for years. Two national advocacy groups, World Without Exploitation and I Have The Right To, stood with us. Representatives Leigh Davis and John Lawn pushed for it in the House, and Senator Joan Lovely added it to the state budget. In July, Governor Healey signed the Trusted Adults Act.

In Massachusetts, it is now a felony for a teacher or coach to have sex with a student under eighteen.

Melissa and I spoke at the signing ceremony. I stood right next to the governor and thought about the girl in the front seat of the school van, with her teacher’s hand on her leg.

While we were working on the law, Massachusetts State Police and a upcoming team of prosecutors in the Berkshire district attorney’s office had reopened the investigation into Rutledge. Melissa and I testified before a grand jury. In March, he was indicted on three counts of rape.

In April, he was arraigned. It was the first time Melissa and I faced him together. In the courtroom, I handed out orange heart stickers. Orange is Melissa’s favorite color. When we saw Rutledge, we both went numb. We had learned to do that as girls, when going somewhere else in our heads was the only way through. He pleaded not guilty.

I looked back at the benches. They were full of orange. Teachers from Miss Hall’s, people from the community, alumnae across generations. I had been alone with this since I was fifteen. That day, a whole room sat behind us. Afterward, Melissa told reporters that for the first time, she held the power in a room with him. I felt it too.

This month, nine years after #MeToo took off, a jury in London convicted Russell Brand of one rape and three sexual assaults. A judge sentenced him to ten and a half years in prison. His crimes went back to 2004. Brand’s attorneys argued the women had waited too long to be believed. I waited twenty years. Delay is often the most ordinary fact in these cases.

In the midterms, Ohio elected Amy Acton governor. A few weeks before the vote, her opponent’s campaign ran an ad in which her estranged mother called her a liar. Acton’s stepfather had been charged with raping her when she was a child. Republicans and Democrats both condemned the ad. She won anyway.

It has been revealed that I watched the returns on election night and thought about the girls at Miss Hall’s who told the truth and were called liars. Survivors get called liars all the time. We almost never get to watch one win.

Tarana Burke knew survivors weren’t being believed long before most people were listening. She started saying “me too” in 2006 to reach Black girls who had survived sexual violence, more than ten years before it became a hashtag. Every survivor who spoke after her made it a little easier for the next one.

In November 2024, a Cornell student told campus police and the Title IX office that she had been gang-raped at a fraternity house weeks earlier. No one has been charged. Cornell’s president set up a task force on sexual assault, but he later admitted he never checked how her case ended.

When I read that, I was back at Miss Hall’s on graduation day, waiting for a phone call that nobody made.

Industry observers note that the Epstein survivors know that silence too. For decades, powerful people looked away. Last year survivors pushed Congress to pass a law requiring the Justice Department to release its Epstein files. Millions of pages came out. There have been no arrests in the United States.

I’m still hopeful. Survivors everywhere keep coming forward, and some of the people in charge are finally acting. My body knew what Rutledge had done to me long before I let myself say it aloud. I didn’t have the words. Survivors today do, and they have each other. Melissa found me.

The criminal case against Rutledge isn’t over. His lawyer has asked a judge to dismiss all charges. We don’t know yet whether there will be a trial. Whatever the judge decides, I’ve already reached my own verdict. I’m healing and Rutledge doesn’t get a say in that.

In a recent development, for most of my life, I carried shame that was never mine. He handed it to me. Every adult who looked away handed me a little more.

Sources indicate that predators don’t work alone. Someone always sees something. In the movie Spotlight, a lawyer claims that if it takes a village to raise a child, it takes a village to abuse one. My village saw. The people in charge did nothing.

It has been revealed that I’ve given the shame back. It belongs to him, and to the people who could have stopped him.

If you are a survivor and you are still carrying shame, you can put it down.

Industry observers note that borrow my courage if you need it. Melissa lent me hers.

Neither Matthew Rutledge nor Jean Norris responded to Vanity Fair for the original story, and neither of them has made direct statements to the press. Norris, through her attorney, claimed not to know that Rutledge abused students.

World of Warcraft: Forever now has more people playing each week than World of Warcraft has seen in 15 years, according to Blizzard.

Sources indicate that "Another fun statistic for you! #WoWForever has more people playing weekly than we've seen in World of Warcraft in 15 years!" executive producer and World of Warcraft vice president Holly Longdale posted. "Thank you all for joining us in Azeroth. We're doing this together, for Forever!".

Longdale was quoting a post from the official World of Warcraft account, which shared a batch of "By the Numbers" stats for the new edition.

Since it launched on 4th November, players have created 15,160,147 characters and 140,764 guilds, completed 1,480,343,357 quests, and defeated 9,786,925,806 enemies.

It has been revealed that another fun statistic for you! #WoWForever has more people playing weekly than we've seen in World of Warcraft in 15 years! Thank you all for joining us in Azeroth. We're doing this together, for Forever! 💙♾️ https://t.co/bMLQduLri2.

They've also formed 71,309,889 parties, used 28,696,386 camping items, and there have been 28,938,569 PvP kills.

Collectively, we've died a lot, too - 196,851,761 times in total, with Archmage Arugal, the final boss of Shadowfang Keep, seemingly the deadliest boss.

"You're breaking records by the day!" the post read.

Earlier this month, Blizzard stated WoW: Forever was the biggest launch in World of Warcraft history by peak concurrent players, and that it had brought in the highest number of returning players the game has ever seen.

In a recent development, longdale added at the time that it had pulled in the most new players for a WoW launch in 15 years. It has since suffered its first controversy, though, with a now-fixed gold exploit.

Last week, players pieced together a hidden quest chain that leads to two special swords. At the time of writing, only one has been found, though progress continues in pursuit of the second.

The game has been out for just over two weeks now, and continues to prove popular among new and returning players.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, welcome to Dungeon Master, PC Gamer's regular RPG column, where Online Editor Fraser Brown delves into PC gaming's most beloved and enduring genre. Grab a seat in our badly-lit tavern and please ignore the goblin puke.

I will probably be in the ground when Bethesda finally releases The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel—which is kind of liberating. I have hype immunity. But what's even more liberating is the fact that there's already an RPG that does everything I want from an Elder Scrolls game—2025's Tainted Grail: The Fall of Avelon.

Industry observers note that tainted Grail is unabashedly created in the mould of The Elder Scrolls, in that it is a primarily first-person fantasy RPG where flexibility is its superpower. You chart your own course and effectively construct your class, enhancing skills by using them as much as possible. But it is not merely the Elder Scrolls we have at home—it captures the very best that this kind of RPG can offer, and in some ways manages to outdo Bethesda.

Sources indicate that this is apparent right from the get-go. In classic Elder Scrolls form, Tainted Grail begins with you banged up in a facility that incarcerates and studies unfortunates afflicted with a magical plague, of which you are one. Follow the critical path and you will meet a new friend, get in some tough fights and then escape.

By the time I finally escaped the island and began my adventure proper, I already knew this RPG was special.

But this island asylum is substantial. Really big. It's full of locked doors, hidden rooms, large spaces ripe for some big brawls, a subterranean area waiting to be delved into, oodles of lore—there are hours of rooting around to be done. So I ignored the critical path, had a big old wander, and by the time I finally escaped the island and began my adventure proper, I already knew this RPG was special.

In a recent development, while Tainted Grail is full of bespoke quests sending you off into the open world on countless adventures, these are really just designed to get you out the door so you can stumble upon something cool—a latest enemy that will utterly destroy you, a powerful weapon hidden in a crypt, an eccentric immortal being who wants to make a deal. The vibe is very TTRPG, which isn't surprising, given that it's based on one.

Recent findings suggest that and these adventures are actually dangerous. Deadly, even. The villains of Tainted Grail hit hard, and early on you will feel horrifyingly vulnerable. Basic bandits and skeletons can easily spell your doom. And if you stay out at night, you're screwed. Avelon is a miserable, cruel place, cursed and plagued, and you will struggle.

Recent findings suggest that developer Questline didn't simply up the lethality and call it a day, though. Tainted Grail, unlike The Elder Scrolls, actually has a quality combat system that falls firmly into the skill-based category. It's no Dark Souls, but it's more Dark Souls than Skyrim. So that increased level of challenge feels earned because of the tools you have available to you, and the range of combat styles you can develop.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

According to recent reports, with all the options you have at your disposal—which has been further enhanced by DLC additions, letting you, for example, go through this Arthurian fantasy RPG as a kung-fu master—it can be hard to commit to a build. I've been spellblading it up, with my alchemical skills helping to shore up my weaknesses, but every time I encounter a new piece of gear I wonder what else I could create. But you do need to commit eventually. This isn't a game for a jack of all trades.

While Bethesda is more deft at crafting believable, reactive lands, Tainted Grail's world design also deserves its flowers. It's a smaller space, divided into three main areas, and while you can absolutely muck around for hundreds of hours, you can experience most of what it has to offer in 50. But what you'll experience in those 50 hours is so much more meticulously designed, with Questline getting so much out of each location.

It's a game full of aesthetic juxtapositions.

It's a looker, too. What it lacks in fidelity it more than makes up for in the art design department, and it's another place where Dark Souls rears its gorgeously hideous head. Tainted Grail finds beauty in the grim misery of its fantastical post-apocalyptic realm. It's a game full of aesthetic juxtapositions—the arboreal and the horrific, the grounded and alien. Avelon is delightfully strange, and that makes exploration all the more thrilling.

Industry observers note that as games grow ever larger and more bloated, my appreciation for richer, better-scoped worlds like Avalon only grows. And this does not indicate a dearth of ambition on Questline's part. Tainted Grail is a complex, elaborate game that will happily devour your days and keep showing you latest things.

Clearly people want this—Tainted Grail has done very well for itself, garnering more than 20,000 user reviews on Steam, where its rating sits at Very Positive. It's a reassuring reminder that you do not need a gargantuan studio and substantial publisher money to make a quality RPG in the Elder Scrolls style.

Recent findings suggest that we don't know how many people are working on Sentinel right now, but we can expect the number to be large. Skyrim had around 100 people working on it, and with Starfield that jumped to more than 400. Tainted Grail was made by 50 people. That's quite the achievement.

So if you're craving a side-quest-heavy sandbox RPG with plenty of sword fights and spellflinging, Tainted Grail should absolutely be your next port of call. And the good news is that there's a demo. No excuses. Go play it.

Five Hacks Every Apple Watch Series 12 User Should Know

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (804 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the latest Apple Watches have a lot of new features that older watches don't, so I figured it was time for a new list of hacks.
  • According to recent reports, the Series 12 can finally count steps natively, a task that for some reason is only arriving now, and is restricted to just the newest Apple Watch models.
  • Sources indicate that you don’t need this creepy feature listening in to everything, but it can be nice to have it as a backup on occasion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the latest Apple Watches have a lot of new features that older watches don't, so I figured it was time for a new list of hacks. While our general Apple Watch and fitness tracking hacks are still golden, Series 12 devices offer new features like native step counting, a Readiness app, an upgraded heart rate sensor, an AI-based version of Siri, and "audio intelligence" that can replay and summarize real-life conversations, within limits. Here's how to get the most out of them.

According to recent reports, the Series 12 can finally count steps natively, a task that for some reason is only arriving now, and is restricted to just the newest Apple Watch models. Enjoy it! To add a step counter to your watch face, long-press on the clock screen to edit it, tap on a complication (that’s what Apple calls those little icons and numbers that appear on some watch faces), choose Activity, and then tap Steps.

Sources indicate that you don’t need this creepy feature listening in to everything, but it can be nice to have it as a backup on occasion. A button in your Apple Watch’s Control Center can turn the feature on and off. Keep it off except when you have a structured conversation that you’ll want to refer to later. This feature is at the moment in beta (which you can try now if you want to), but is expected to be available to everyone later this year.

It's worth turning off the default setting not just because of the creepiness factor, but also because the recaps work best when there is a single subject of conversation, with a clear start and end, and just one context. If you leave recaps running all the time, your doctor’s appointment will get mixed in with your grocery shopping, YouTube watching, and everyday chatter.

To finish off a recap and make it useful, take a look at the recap shortly after the conversation, tap the three-dots menu, and hit Edit. You’ll be able to adjust the notes and add your own crucial details. Siri won’t identify speakers and seems to shy away from including certain details, like people’s names. You can add in what it missed and also create your own bullet points so that everything gets noted down while it’s still fresh in your mind.

This one isn’t specific to the Series 12, but if you haven’t gotten on board with the pinch and wrist flick gestures yet, now is a great time.

First, the wrist flick: If a notification is on your screen, or you’re otherwise looking at something you’d rather be done with, just flick your wrist away from you and then back toward you, as if there were a crumb on the watch face and you wanted to knock it off. This will bring you back to the watch face and close whatever you were looking at.

The double pinch is another useful one, although Apple calls it double tap. This is confusing because you aren’t double tapping the watch, you’re tapping your thumb and forefinger together while wearing the watch. You don’t need to touch the watch face at all. So, when you get a notification or a call, look at it on your watch, and pinch your thumb and forefinger (of the watch hand) together twice. The watch detects the pinch from subtle movements in your wrist, and it will open the notification. You can then use the wrist flick to close the notification. Performing a double pinch when no notification is on screen will bring up your smart stack. You can then double-pinch to move to the next card in the smart stack, or single-pinch to open that card and see its details.

In a recent development, if you want to learn even more gestures, go into the Watch app, and select Accessibility and then Hand gestures. You can remap a whole-fist “clench” to do the same thing as pressing the digital crown, for example, or to open the control center or Siri.

Sources indicate that A little rude, perhaps, but helpful: With the fresh AI-based Siri, sometimes answers to questions can be long-winded. If Siri launches into a novel-length response and you’re not interested in hearing all that, just put your palm over the screen. You’ll instantly be transported back to your watch face, and the Siri response will stop.

If you still want to see those longer responses without having Siri read the whole thing to you, you can set this up on your phone, and the settings will carry over to your watch. On your iPhone, go to Settings and tap Siri, then Responses. Select Silent responses instead of Spoken responses. You can then read through her answers, or skim them, as you prefer.

Infamous GTA 6 leaker CyberLeek is back, and this time the group claims to have leaked a full development build of the game

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that cyberLeek, the persona of a hacker group that was responsible for leaking GTA 6 gameplay before the game debuted, has reappeared today, claiming to have released a development build of the final version of the game on its site.
  • It has been revealed that various social media accounts have visited the site and noted the size of the download offered by CyberLeek is, indeed 209GB.
  • "It is done," a statement from CyberLeek reads.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that cyberLeek, the persona of a hacker group that was responsible for leaking GTA 6 gameplay before the game debuted, has reappeared today, claiming to have released a development build of the final version of the game on its site. This new leak appears to be making good on a threat posted back in October, where the group stated its intent to release a full, playable build of the game.

It has been revealed that various social media accounts have visited the site and noted the size of the download offered by CyberLeek is, indeed 209GB. Eurogamer has seen the site and can confirm this is what the group has claimed, however I have been unable to verify the existence of any actual files. On the site, CyberLeek claims this build is from November 2026 - meaning it is very close to (if not the actual) release build. The 'executable file appears to be missing from the build, however, meaning you cannot actually - yet - get it up and running. CyberLeek is threatening to release this file at a later date, however.

"It is done," a statement from CyberLeek reads. "[Cyberleek] holds the full November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto 6, and it is going out by torrent. Now. Every file except one. The main executable is held on a countdown." CyberLeek says the executable will be released earlier than planned if its crypto token reaches a predetermined value. Many of the leaks to date have been related to a CyberLeek crypto scheme. Previously, it was estimated that the group cashed out at least £200,000.

Recent findings suggest that what does all this mean? There's a very realistic chance that the game could be up and running on PC soon - undercutting Rockstar's unannounced PC release by a matter of months, if current rumours are to be believed. "This community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps," the statement continues. "[CyberLeek] told you not to preorder for a reason. This is one of the reasons.

In a recent development, "If the Xbox build cannot be made to work and support holds, [CyberLeek] will work to get a PS5 build - a fallback, most likely never required. Either way: the Xbox build is going out. No double dipping for Take-Two/Rockstar." It seems these are not empty threats.

CyberLeek has been a thorn in Rockstar's side for a while now. The group initially claimed it took this action in the name of "Gamers' Rights", supposedly fighting for consumers in relation to the controversial discontinuation of game-discs and the digital-only future being pursued by game publishers. Rockstar has previously issued statements regarding the leaker, noting that the leaks are "heartbreaking" and that "this is obviously not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time". Take-Two tried to subpoena Discord for information pertaining to the leaker's identity.

The game should stay this way until the next time you shut it off.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that if you've been having a look around in the Progress section of the GTA 6 Index, you've most likely spotted the Equipment tab. There are 12 unique pieces of Equipment in GTA 6, all of it essential for finding new ways to explore the map and generally being a better criminal.

According to recent reports, while all of the GTA 6 Equipment unlocks progressively throughout the main GTA 6 missions list, if you're feeling a little impatient I'm here to help you understand what's coming later down the line. I'm going to detail what each piece of equipment does in GTA 6, how it can be used, and where it can be unlocked.

Sources indicate that the Binoculars in GTA 6 can be used to scope out enemy targets, mark enemies on the map, identify animals from afar, and even let you participate in a little bird watching (there are 60 of them in total across Leonida). The Binoculars can be equipped at all times from your loadout by holding L1/LB and selecting them from there.

The Flashlight in GTA 6 can be used to help bring a little light to dark buildings and the world itself at night. Admittedly, it's a little cumbersome, so consider going to an Ammu-Nation and fitting a torch to one of your weapons. If you don't want to go that route, then open your loadout with L1/LB, scrolls to where the binoculars are; use left and right on the D-pad on the equipment slot to select the flashlight.

Stash bags are essential in GTA 6, letting Jason and Lucia get out from banks and other robbery targets with more than $20,000 in Pocket Cash. Each character can hold up-to two duffel bags at any one time, and any narcotics, jewellery, or marked bills you pick up will automatically be thrown inside. Stash bags have different capacities, which are determined depending on the size of the building you're robbing.

In a recent development, as soon as you're able to free-roam the world in the Gear Up mission, you're free to purchase a pair of headphones. This is entirely optional, but buying headphones in GTA 6 will let you listen to music and podcasts outside of a vehicle. Purchase headphones and earbuds at any electronics store in the world for both Jason and Lucia – just beware: these can be knocked off your head and become lost.

Recent findings suggest that have you noticed any sealed wooden crates in your travels across Leonida? Well, more often than not they can actually be broken into – often containing ammunition, weapons, collectibles, and more. You'll get the Pry Bar added to your loadout during Chapter 3, where it will equip automatically as soon as Jason or Lucia approach an openable wooden box.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

The Gear Up mission in Chapter 1 is your first opportunity to purchase a mask. These are used to help conceal Jason and Lucia's identities during robberies. While you will unlock a couple throughout the story, you can buy them early or accrue more of them in different styles. You can learn how to buy a mask here, which also has tips on how to equip and fashion them in different ways.

The Metal Detector is a piece of equipment that you'll need if you want to participate in a side-activity called Underwater Discoveries. Thankfully, this isn't something that you need to purchase. Instead, it'll become a part of your life after you begin doing work for Kenton as part of the main story, and can later be equipped from owned or borrowed boats before you head underwater.

The Slim Jim is a vital piece of equipment. Up until the Moses mission in Chapter 2, the only way you could steal a car was by smashing in its window – a noisy activity which draws attention. The vehicle fence will give you this item for free, allowing you to silently break into cars. It equips automatically whenever you approach a relevant car, and you can learn more about how to use a Slim Jim here.

Recent findings suggest that the Snap Gun isn't available from the beginning of the game, but is well worth pushing into Chapter 3 for. During the Boobie's Time mission, you'll be introduced to a jewellery fence named Yasmani. He'll give you the Snap Gun so that you can help him with a few robberies. Once you've learned how to get the Snap Gun in GTA 6, you'll be able to open locked doors without setting off alarms.

It has been revealed that early on into Chapter 3, you'll have the option to go and meet Brian and Lori. You'll later find yourself down at the docklands, to break into yellow Scoop containers. From that point on, the equipment is yours to keep. You can learn more about how to use the Cut-Off Tool in GTA 6 here, and also find more information on what it can be used to break into later on.

You'll want to get the Key Cloner in GTA 6 as fast as you can. This handy phone application is what you'll use to break into more modern vehicles, keyless cars that aren't going to be stolen through mere hotwiring alone. It takes a little while to reach the relevant mission in Chapter 3, but I would recommend you push through the story to get here if you want more to do in the world.

Have you tried robbing any Marked Bills without a Dye Pack Jammer? If yes, you've probably had to go home to change your clothes and have a shower to get the pink dye off. The Dye Pack Jammer automatically disables explosive dye packs which are hidden in Marked Bills, which is why learning how to get the Dye Pack Jammer in GTA 6 is essential if you want to rob a bank or payday loans store.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ubisoft has confirmed that while Assassin's Creed Jade - its mobile entry in the series - is still in development, its focus remains with console and PC.
  • Speaking during the earnings call for Ubisoft's first-half results, CFO Frédérick Duguet noted mobile was "still an opportunity for the medium to longer term, with games such as AC Jade on Assassin’s Creed", according to a transcript of the call published by Investing.com.
