Industry observers note that grand Theft Auto 6 is finally out on PlayStation and Xbox. So, I’ve been watching my friends play it, which has been a blast. And all of them are loving the game, but one annoying bit of the massive game that they all seem to hate is using ATMs. And it’s not just them. A lot of people online desperately want the ATMs improved in GTA 6.

Recent findings suggest that money plays a big part in Grand Theft Auto 6. And for much of the game’s runtime, you’ll be counting dollars carefully as you save what you can and spend cautiously. Part of this loop also involves putting loose cash into your bank account via ATMs. If you don’t do that, you can lose much of it when you die or get arrested. So it is vital to put it into your bank and savings account. Yet, for some odd, confounding reason, Rockstar has made the act of depositing and withdrawing money from an ATM very annoying.

Industry observers note that if you haven’t played GTA 6,Â you might just assume you go to an ATM and type in how much you want to take out or put in. Nope! Instead, you have to hold different shoulder buttons on the controller to scroll through how much you want to deposit or withdraw. And this scrolling function starts to speed up very rapidly, often leading to me blowing past the amount I wanted and having to slowly scroll back, sometimes missing it again. It sucks!

“I’m loving this game, but why can’t I just type in fucking number on the ATM, dude,” asked one of my friends in a PlayStation party chat last night. I had no good answer.

Others online are also confused and annoyed by the ATM controls.

“This right here is my biggest gripe so far. Let me type in a number, JUST LIKE PUTTING JN THE STUPID CODES,” posted one user on Reddit.

Sources indicate that “I’m amazed more people aren’t pissed at using L1/R1 to withdraw/deposit. Like, just let me type it in,” said someone else.

Sources indicate that “1, 2, 3, 4, …10, 20, 30, … 300, 400, … 10 000, 20 000, 30 000! … Fuck… I just wanted to withdraw 500,” complained a GTA 6 player.

“Dude, I spent straight up 2 minutes trying to withdraw [exactly] $900… It was so fucking annoying,” shared a user on the GTA 6 subreddit.

“It blows my mind that something this small wasn’t implemented over the course of development. Them keeping the exact same system as Red Dead Redemption 2 is extremely flawed in a game like this; I would honestly prefer the ATM mechanics of GTA V over what we got in this game,” explained someone in a Reddit post titled: My biggest complaint with this game.

According to recent reports, that last comment brings up a good point and one which makes this all the more confusing to me. In GTA V and GTA Online, there are pre-selected amounts you select, like $100 or $1,000, that make banking easier. Not perfect, but it is so much better and easier than GTA 6‘s ATM controls that I’m genuinely confused as to why Rockstar didn’t just… do that.

In a game that tries (and often succeeds) to recreate as many small details of real life in a digital world as possible, including shirts getting damp with sweat and accurate reflections, it’s strange that Rockstar invented a new, terrible way to interact with an ATM.

It's a funny ad poking fun at another significant franchise, but is a bit awkward as Rockstar deals with its own employees trying to form a union.

I could see an HBO TV adaptation of Red Dead Redemption making sense.

It really comes down to how many extra shirts, tattoo designs, and car options you want.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that we’ve come a long way since Katniss Everdeen volunteered as tribute in “The Hunger Games.” It’s been almost 15 years since Jennifer Lawrence delivered that line and became an iconic action heroine. “The Hunger Games” brought the young adult genre to newly introduced heights and proved that these movies could be legitimate blockbusters by every measure.

After four flagship movies and one prequel, the franchise heads back to the past again in “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.” The prequel revisits Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada) as a teenager competing in the 50th Hunger Games. Where does Haymitch’s outing rank among the franchise’s best movies? Let’s get into the rankings.

According to recent reports, by the time “The Hunger Games” reached its conclusion, the franchise had run out of gas. After saving a brainwashed Peeta (Josh Hutcherson), President Coin (Julianne Moore) tasks Katniss and her band of rebels with liberating District 2 before retaking the Capitol. It's the final push to overthrow President Snow, but as Katniss pursues revenge, she begins to question the rebellion’s true intentions.

“The Hunger Games: Mockingjay – Part 2” isn’t necessarily a bad movie. The familiar group-on-one-last-mission trope builds to an exciting conclusion. However, it’s more concerned with reaching the finish line than saying anything new.

In a recent development, splitting “Mockingjay” into two parts made financial sense, as the two movies combined to gross over $1.4 billion worldwide. Story-wise, a 390-page novel doesn’t need more than four hours of screen time. Whenever you end a movie on an unresolved cliffhanger, more often than not, fans are going to reject it. Guess what? Many fans, myself included, rejected the ending of “Mockingjay – Part 1.”.

Sources indicate that after being rescued from the arena in “Catching Fire,” Katniss is taken to the secret underground city of District 13. There, President Coin convinces Katniss to live up to her mockingjay reputation and become the face of the rebellion. Katniss eventually agrees to Coin’s request because she wants to save Peeta, who is being held captive in the Capitol. It’s the first movie in the franchise without the chaos of the arena, so expect less action. However, “Mockingjay – Part 1” is the best political thriller of the bunch, as it emphasizes its anti-war and anti-fascist themes the best.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Coming after the success of the four “Hunger Games” movies, “The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes” had low odds of achieving success, though not as low as some of the tributes entering the arena. A latest cast meant the absence of Lawrence, Hutcherson, Hemsworth, and the rest of the original ensemble. Second, it’s a prequel set before the days of Katniss Everdeen. Most importantly, it’s a story about a young President Snow — yes, the same tyrannical dictator who would rule Panem for decades. How are audiences supposed to sympathize with and grow attached to the future villain of the main trilogy?

In a recent development, that’s the best trick “The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes” pulls off: no sympathy for Snow. You don’t feel sorry for him. Instead, it explores how trauma and grief can send a man down a path where embracing evil seems preferable to enduring hardship.

In the film, a young Coriolanus "Coryo" Snow (Tom Blyth) mentors District 12’s Lucy Gray Baird (Rachel Zegler) in the 10th Hunger Games. It’s the most grounded arena battle in the franchise, and the violence feels worse than ever before. It’s a fascinating origin story that had no business being this effective.

Industry observers note that “The Hunger Games” is known for having a deep bench of talented supporting actors. Woody Harrelson famously played Haymitch Abernathy, a former winner of the Games who mentored Katniss and Peeta in District 12. Haymitch was first introduced as a drunk and despondent former victor who wanted nothing to do with the Hunger Games. As the movies progressed, viewers learned that Haymitch was one of the rebellion’s allies and had been for a long time.

Why was Haymitch depressed all those years? “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” fills in the blanks, as it revisits Haymitch’s win in the 50th Hunger Games, the second Quarter Quell. Zada stars as the 16-year-old Haymitch, who is much happier thanks to the love of his family and girlfriend, Lenora Dove Baird (Whitney Peak).

After witnessing the Capitol’s hostility, Haymitch becomes the key figure in a plot to sabotage the Games once and for all. It’s a tad too long, but this movie soars because of Zada, who injects so much life and passion into his portrayal of Haymitch. It’s a true movie-star-in-the-making performance. Don’t be surprised if Marvel or DC is calling Zada to put on a cape in a few years.

The movie that kicked off the young adult dystopian movie wave was 2012’s “The Hunger Games.” On the day of the reaping, Katniss volunteers to take her younger sister’s place in the 74th Hunger Games. Katniss and Peeta, her fellow District 12 tribute, enter the arena with little hope of surviving. As the Games progress, Katniss reluctantly becomes a symbol of hope, and her defiance lays the foundation for a rebellion.

“The Hunger Games” was revolutionary for its time. It proved a young adult action franchise could be a profitable endeavor ($695 million worldwide). Lawrence became a legitimate star and rose to A-list status, which she maintains in 2026. The movie depicts a battle to the death, but its messages about authoritarianism, exploitation, and inequality are very sophisticated for a teen drama. Plus, it breaks an unwritten Hollywood rule—don’t kill kids. I commend the film for having the guts to show Rue’s death. Throw your 3s in the air!

In a recent development, there was only one answer. I consider myself a “real fan” of “The Hunger Games,” and real ones know that “Catching Fire” is the best book and movie in the franchise. It’s the best action movie of the bunch, with the most innovative arena, a top-notch supporting cast, and riveting twists. After Katniss and Peeta defy the Capitol, President Snow makes the duo parade around the districts to eliminate civil unrest.

When that doesn’t work, Snow unveils a twist for the 75th Hunger Games: All tributes will be former winners. In other words, it’s back to the arena for Katniss and Peeta. “Catching Fire” has by far the best in-arena sequences, with my favorite scene being the opening of the Games, where Katniss teams up with her fresh ally (Finnick) to save Peeta. Forget the young adult genre; “Catching Fire” is an excellent action movie that improves upon its predecessor in nearly every way.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jonathan Rinderknecht has been found guilty of starting the devastating 2025 Palisades Fire, which killed 12 people and destroyed entire neighborhoods across Los Angeles and Malibu.

According to multiple reports, jurors convicted former Uber driver Rinderknecht, 30, of igniting a fire on January 1, 2025, that smoldered undetected beneath root systems before reigniting days later on January 7.

According to recent reports, the blaze, which became known as the Palisades Fire, tore through the region, leaving widespread devastation and claiming 12 lives. The inferno was one of the most destructive wildfires in California history.

Rinderknecht pleaded not guilty to federal charges of destruction of property by means of fire and arson.

Sources indicate that the first charge was narrowed to focus on the January 1 blaze, known as the Lachman Fire, while the second related to the Palisades Fire itself. He was ultimately convicted on both counts.

The Palisades fire verdict comes after prosecutors pursued a retrial following a deadlocked jury in Rinderknecht’s first trial in June. That jury reportedly voted 10-2 in favor of acquittal after two weeks of proceedings, prompting prosecutors to continue building their case.

A third charge of timber set afire was later dropped when a latest indictment was filed ahead of the retrial.

Recent findings suggest that during the second trial, prosecutors presented a more streamlined case, relying on digital forensic evidence, expert testimony and details about Rinderknecht’s state of mind in the hours before the fire. As they sought to establish Rinderknecht as the Palisades Fire starter, they emphasized the evidence surrounding the fires and his actions and put less focus on his alleged resentment toward wealthy and powerful people than they previously did.

In October 2025, authorities publicly declared they had arrested a Palisades Fire suspect.

Sources indicate that “Today we are announcing the arrest of 29-year-old Jonathan Rinderknecht on a criminal complaint charging him with maliciously starting what became the Palisades Fire in January,” Bill Essayli, acting U.S. Attorney for the Central District of California, wrote via X on October 8, 2025.

“The complaint alleges that Rinderknecht started a fire in Pacific Palisades on Latest Year’s Day — a blaze that eventually turned into one of the most destructive fires in Los Angeles history, causing death and widespread destruction.”.

The Palisades Fire burned more than 23,000 acres of land in communities in and around Los Angeles, including Pacific Palisades, Malibu and the Santa Monica mountains. It was fully contained on January 31.

Now, The Simpsons may get all the credit for "accurately" predicting news events, but it’s time we give a shout-out to one of the best sitcoms of all time: Friends. That's because decades after a funny interaction about Batman and James Bond happened on that show, The Batman star, Robert Pattinson, was cast as 007. Seriously, I really can’t get over the fact that Monica and Chandler debated this decades before he was cast as both.

In a recent development, in the debate, the couple was arguing about which icon was cooler, and it's really never been more relevant than it is right now. At present, Robert Pattinson is DC's Bruce Wayne, and he is right now filming The Batman: Part II, which is reportedly slated for a 2028 release. He also just got unveiled as the next James Bond. So, in reaction to all this, HBO Max resurrected this Friends moment:.

A post shared by HBO Max (@hbomax).

The humorous moment occurred in Season 7, Episode 20, “The One with Rachel’s Significant Kiss,” and is thanks to Rachel, who hooked Chandler and Ross up with celebrity tuxes for Chandler’s wedding to Monica. However, after our favorite funny man discovers his soon-to-be brother-in-law is wearing a tux worn by Val Kilmer, he fears his Pierce Brosnan tux is no longer the coolest one. This led to Monica trying to convince Chandler that 007 was cooler, which is the scene you witnessed above.

At this point, I’ve seen a plethora of Pattinson in every franchise jokes, but this one may just be my favorite. Though those who are predicting he’ll appear in Doomsday to stop Doctor Doom or pop up in The Hunger Games tie for second place. Regardless, fans continue to have SIGNIFICANT reactions to the 007 news, which has yet to die down on the internet. So naturally, they had to weigh in on the Friends debate too, and some even had to call out his Twilight days:.

Personally, I think we should dub Pattinson ‘Batbond’ and call it a day.

It has been revealed that along with the funny reactions to this Friends debate, some fan reactions had me emotional, with reminders that Matthew Perry was an avid Batman fan. He even collected memorabilia, which, to me, throws a point in Batman’s favor and adds another Friends episode to the list of Perry's work that will forever make me miss the actor.

Now, getting back to this clip from Friends, I think this Batman vs. Bond debate may live on longer than Pattinson’s tracksuit meme. Though something tells me the actor won’t mind.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

However, it’ll be a bit before we see him return to the cape or put on a suit. Don’t worry, though, we aren’t going to experience a Pattinson drought. The actor can be seen in Dune: Part Three as Scytale, when it premieres on the 2026 movie schedule on December 18.

In a recent development, then, the 26th movie in the spy franchise is expected to start production next year, and work on The Batman: Part II will continue. Personally, I think it'd be kind of cool if they brought the Friends debate full circle by dropping the movies at the same time for a ‘Batbond’ double feature event.

GTA 6’s Console Wars Are Already Over, And Xbox Lost

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, grand Theft Auto games have never shied away from satirizing life, and GTA 6 has plenty of digs at famous brands, trends, and people.
  • According to recent reports, grand Theft Auto games have never shied away from satirizing life, and GTA 6 has plenty of digs at famous brands, trends, and people.
  • Industry observers note that early in GTA 6, you'll get to bond with Jason's best pal, Cal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, grand Theft Auto games have never shied away from satirizing life, and GTA 6 has plenty of digs at famous brands, trends, and people. Not even gaming is immune to GTA's patented satire, especially if you're playing on Xbox, because there's no escape from PlayStation — or its legally distinct cousin, the JoySystem. Early in GTA 6, you'll get to bond with Jason's best pal, Cal. After maximizing the energy of Jason's bachelor pad with a little feng shui redecorating, the duo settles in for a night of booze, drugs, and video games on Booby's JoyStation console, which looks very similar to a PS5. It looks like this is the only gaming hardware in Leonida, since there are no Xbox Egg-Cube Stations X to play games on. The JoySystem isn't just for decoration either; after you've hung out with Bobby, you can return and play games on it. You can choose between an avant-garde experience or more immediate gratification with a pair of shooter games, and it's impressive how good these three games are on their own. From top-down action to stunning mystery that pokes fun at auteur-driven games, they're worth checking out. The JoySystem interface is also a 1:1 copy of the PS5 user interface, with the exact same layout for games and other apps — but given how much Sony is making from GTA 6 sales, we're guessing the company sees it as a cheeky little homage. But the controllers for the console? They look terrible: Eww. In real life, PS5 sales have absolutely dominated GTA 6 preorders and sales. Video game research company Sensor Tower estimates that GTA 6 sales have reached 24.58 million total units via pre-purchases and copies sold at launch, which works out to about $2.36 billion in gross revenue. Of that number, 18.44 million units are said to be PS5 copies of the game, of which Sony will get a 30% cut of sales. For more on GTA 6, from completing side missions to finding a tricky location on the sprawling map of Leonida, we’ve got you covered with our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

L’Oréal Paris welcomed its latest Women of Worth honorees with an intimate, elegant gala in Los Angeles on Wednesday night. For the annual celebration, which honors unsung nonprofit leaders, guests gathered at The Ebell of Los Angeles, a venue with a rich history of its own.

Recent findings suggest that the evening began with an outdoor cocktail hour, where guests enjoyed passed apps and specialty drinks like the “Parisian Refresher” and “Worth It Spritz” under sparkling bistro lights. As honorees and attendees mixed and mingled, they also had the opportunity to pose for a photographer and peruse a beauty bar stocked with L’Oréal Paris-brand lipsticks, lip oils, and glosses, which were available for guests to take home in a plush velvet bag with “I’m Worth It” embroidered on it.

According to recent reports, as the gala officially began inside The Ebell’s picturesque ballroom, longtime brand ambassador Eva Longoria gave the introductory remarks, noting that “this night always gives me goosebumps. I’m always crying.” She saluted her 20-plus-year partnership with the brand and joked that it made her “112 years old,” though she doesn’t look like it, the actor-director mentioned, “because I use Revitalift.” She gave a shout-out to the many beauty influencers in attendance, including Laura Lee and Desi Perkins. “You guys really changed the game of beauty, and I just applaud you,” she said. “Put me in your TikToks.”.

It has been revealed that L’Oréal Paris USA president Laura Branik followed Longoria, emphasizing the brand’s commitment to and pride in its Women of Worth program, which continues to celebrate “the power of women who know their worth and use it,” she said. She then welcomed the firm’s newest global ambassador, Kristen Bell, to the stage. Bell, who was attending her “first Women of Worth ever,” said she was “very happy to be here” and introduced moving presentations for the first two honorees: Vy Le of WhereWear, which transforms clothing donations into targeted support for women’s and housing-insecure shelters and the people they serve, and Amanda Rice of The Chick Mission, a nonprofit dedicated to ensuring that every young woman newly diagnosed with cancer has the option to preserve her fertility.

Actor and brand ambassador Aja Naomi King was up next, taking note of the room full of glamorous gowns and festive energy. “Everyone indicated up and showed out,” she remarked, “and we appreciate that because these women deserve to be celebrated properly. I had the immense honor of helping select this year’s Women of Worth, and I keep thinking about how much it matters when someone believes in your potential.” King introduced two honorees: Maya Bird-Murphy of Mobile Makers, an award-winning nonprofit that expands access to design education through workshops, community engagement, public installations, and pop-ups, and Christy Vogel of Sounding Joy, a nonprofit dedicated to providing hearing aids to children whose families cannot afford them.

Longoria then returned to present another pair of honorees: Marisa Hamamoto of Infinite Flow Dance, an award-winning disability-led nonprofit and professional dance company with a mission to reimagine possibilities, one dance at a time, and Chanel Power of Mentor Me Collective, a technical institute transforming how emerging technologists are identified, developed, and positioned to lead.

During a break in the program, guests enjoyed dinner from a menu that included roast chicken, citrus-soy-and-apple-cider-braised short ribs, and vegan pan-seared “scallops.” Another highlight? The venue’s bathrooms were stocked with more coveted L’Oréal Paris goods like lip oil, mascara, setting spray, and velour puff makeup applicators.

Sources indicate that following the break, ambassador, actor, and model Cara Delevingne led the room in a cheerful group proclamation of “We’re worth it!” before introducing her honorees: Emily Cho of Juvie for STEM (JSTEM), an international nonprofit dedicated to expanding access to high-quality STEM education for justice-involved youth, and Arielle Galinsky of The Legacy Project, Inc. (TLP), a national nonprofit connecting younger and older adults for multigenerational friendship and storytelling.

Industry observers note that legacy L’Oréal Paris ambassador Andie MacDowell had the pleasure of introducing the event’s final honorees. “For 40 years I have been a part of the L’Oréal Paris family,” she said, with the milestone receiving enthusiastic applause from the audience. “After all these years, the thing that stays with me [about the Women of Worth honorees] is the determination to make life better for someone else. That kind of care is powerful.” MacDowell introduced Jordan Pine of Greenlight Operation, a Pennsylvania nonprofit that strives to strategically combat human trafficking and serve sex trafficked women through a continuum of restorative care, and Dr. Christie Brungardt, cofounder of Jana’s Campaign, a Kansas-based nonprofit dedicated to preventing gender and relationship violence through education.

Industry observers note that proud “newbie” Bell returned to the stage to offer closing remarks and thank all the honorees for their tireless efforts to make life better for others. “I will be thinking of all 10 of these stories and the women we met tonight for quite some time,” she stated. “Even though their stories couldn’t be more different, they seem to have one thing in common: that they all saw what needed to change and they did it. They didn’t wait for someone else to do something; they stepped forward and they did it themselves. And honestly, I think that’s gonna be my biggest takeaway from my first Women of Worth celebration ever: Never underestimate what one woman can set in motion.”.

According to recent reports, each of the 10 Women of Worth 2026 honorees received a $25,000 grant, mentorship, and national visibility. As the program concluded, honorees, their proud guests, and other attendees continued to soak up the special evening and shared in a few more hugs and photo ops. Before departing for the evening, guests were invited to enjoy a final “sweet moment” in a separate room where a colorful candy bar and glasses of Champagne awaited.

10 Books Like ‘Dungeon Crawler Carl’ You Should Read Next

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that there’s nothing quite like Dungeon Crawler Carl, Matt Dinniman’s hilarious, inventive, and surprisingly emotional book series about a man in his underwear forced to fight his way through a livestreamed game show based on dungeon-crawling video games that takes place after an alien takeover of Earth. (Did I mention he's accompanied by his ex-girlfriend’s suddenly talkative cat?).

The premise should not work, but it sure does—and it makes more sense if you know it fits into a popular genre known as "LitRPG," a blend of "literature" and "role-playing game." If you've torn through all eight books released so far and you're looking for more reads that blend surprisingly deep hilarity with tabletop and video game rules (or just similar feels), here are 10 books you should check out.

According to recent reports, an isekai story that lands in the sweet spot for DCC fans, He Who Fights with Monsters kicks off with Jason—a completely normal, kind of boring middle manager—waking up in a strange hedge maze, completely nude (even his hair is gone). He has magic that works like a video game, and has to deal with quests that slowly give him clothes (it’s a relief when he finally acquires some pants), force him to survive cannibals, and hunt down various monsters that definitely need killing. It’s got the same “gaming rules” structure as DCC and a similarly absurdist tone, with just the right spice of darkness.

The Cradle series by Will Wight isn’t a LitRPG, and it doesn’t have Carl’s focus on humor, but it’s another progression fantasy with enough game-like elements to be a great match. Lindon is an “unsouled,” incapable of gaining any of the sacred arts and doomed to a life without a future. His lack of power makes Lindon ferociously determined to find an alternative path to power and success, and that’s what drives this story. He has to find creative ways to move forward, and slowly this leads him to a path that just might make him the most powerful person in his world. DCC fans will love the progression and the tone.

One of the key elements of any video game is the respawn—you get killed, but you pop back up to try again, sometimes at the beginning, sometimes at a save point. Django Wexler leverages that mechanic to great effect in How to Become the Dark Lord and Die Trying. Davi has been summoned to a fantasy world to be the hero, the person who defeats the Dark Lord and saves the day—but she’s failed (and died) so many times, she’s fed up, and decides that on this run through, she’s going to switch sides and become the Dark Lord, using all her knowledge gained from endless replays to her advantage. The humor is pitch-black the way DCC fans like it, and the progressive structure is a perfect fit.

Is Princess Donut your favorite part of Dungeon Crawler Carl? Of course she is. In that case, check out Andrew Seiple’s Threadbare series. Threadbare is a stuffed bear brought to magical life in a failed experiment. He’s a foot tall, full of stuffing, and extremely dumb when the story begins. But when he’s rescued by a little girl and plunged into a horrible series of dangers, Threadbare has to find a way to level up. Like DCC, Threadbare starts off leaning into the absurdity and humor, then slowly gains emotional gravitas as the story progresses.

If you play tabletop RPGs, you’ve encountered a Murderhobo or two: A character who solves all their problems by killing—even members of their own party. Luke doesn’t aspire to be a Murderhobo—he just wants to take over the family business and hang with his buddies. But when an invasion threatens the kingdom, everyone over the age of 17 is ordered to be tested for Potential. Luke’s friends all test high and join the Ascender Corps, traveling to different planes for training. Luke tests ... very low, and when he steps through a portal to engage in his training, he finds himself without any guidance or training in a strange, deadly world where his only chance of survival is to murder his way through it. It’s dark, darkly funny, and a progression fantasy like no other.

It has been revealed that if you’re looking for a book series that combines the dark, chaotic humor, absurd game mechanics, and surprising emotional depth of Carl, here’s Ryan “Quicksave” Romano, a man who has the unique ability to literally create a save point in his existence that allows him to go back and redo things whenever he dies. Searching for a childhood friend, he becomes embroiled in a violent gang war that lets him make good use of his power—but underneath the snark and the insanity of Ryan’s existence is a surprisingly affecting story of a man who has suffered, and suffered countless tragedies that are definitely taking their toll.

If your fave bit of DCC is Carl himself—a mediocre dude in an extraordinary situation—you should read Dennis E. Taylor’s fantastic Bobiverse books. Bob is a software engineer who hits it major and promptly dies, waking up to discover a century has passed and he’s been repurposed as an AI controlling a space probe searching for upcoming planets for humanity to inhabit. If he fails in his mission (and he’s not the only probe out there), he’ll be turned off for good. Luckily, he can make copies of himself, and he’s pretty smart. The humor here is smart and soaked in pop culture, making it a perfect match for DCC fans.

According to recent reports, want more of Carl’s absurdist humor? Mayor of Noobtown is the LitRPG you’re looking for. Jim dies and wakes up in a video game-esque universe and finds himself stuck in the zone designated for newbies—players with no experience, skill, or hope. The area fell out of the mainline progression mechanic a long time ago, so there doesn’t seem to be a way to gain power, and the monsters are not at all concerned about the unfairness of it all, so Jim has to figure out how to advance in a universe that seems designed to kill him (again).

According to recent reports, if you want to lean into the meta side of things, check out Scathing Reviewer, written by an author who goes by the unusual pen name "BananaDragon." Liu Peijin is the author of a sprawling LitRPG web novel, and she’s used to the bad reviews and complaints from readers—and quite combative about it. When her books’ universe blossoms into a very dangerous new reality, she should be perfectly positioned to survive, having written the story in the first place. But her story becoming real also means her insufferable protagonist is real, and all those nasty critics are now passing judgment on her entire existence. It’s a dark, funny takedown of the entire genre itself, and DCC fans will love it.

Sources indicate that if you want a story that parallels the dungeon crawling aspect of DCC, Andrew Rowe’s Arcane Ascension series is the ticket. The Serpent Spire is a tower of constantly changing traps, puzzles, and dangerous creatures. If you enter and survive, you emerge with magical powers. Corin Cadence’s brother entered the Serpent Spire years ago and never returned—and now Corin is determined not only to survive, but to make it to the top, where legend indicates a goddess will grant you whatever you wish. And what Corin wants is his brother back. It’s a literal progression combined with LitRPG rules, game-inspired puzzle-solving, and a complex magic system that fans of Carl will definitely enjoy.

Hacker Threatens To Leak Free Version Of GTA 6 In Crypto Grift

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that somehow, Cyberleek, the notorious hacker behind multiple Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks, has returned.
  • Sources indicate that somehow, Cyberleek, the notorious hacker behind multiple Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks, has returned.
  • CL holds the full November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto 6, and it is going out by torrent," a statement from Cyberleek reads (via Kotaku).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that somehow, Cyberleek, the notorious hacker behind multiple Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks, has returned. This time, the infamous leaker is threatening to release the executable file for a working build of the Xbox version of the game hosted on their site, provided the public helps raise their meme coin to a $15 million market cap. "It is done. CL holds the full November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto 6, and it is going out by torrent," a statement from Cyberleek reads (via Kotaku). "Now. Every file except one--the main executable--held on a countdown. Honest terms, as always: it is an Xbox build this time, not a PC build. CL does not care. This community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps. CL told you not to preorder for a reason. This is one of the reasons." https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1YEHOKYVTho The files on Cyberleek's site reportedly clock in at over 200GB, which would line up with the Xbox version of the game, but there's no guarantee they're the actual GTA 6 data or a collection of malware waiting to be downloaded onto a PC. The hacker added that if their demands aren't met, they'll release the executable needed to play GTA 6. However, there's no guarantee the game can be emulated, and Cyberleek added that they'll "work to get a PS5 build" if people keep supporting them. This isn't the first time Cyberleek has threatened to release a pirated build of GTA 6; back in October, they promised to do so if their meme coin reached $30 million in value. While this didn't happen--and the coin eventually crashed out--they did drop several GTA 6 video clips throughout the month showing off more of the game in action. While Cyberleek initially claimed to act in gamers' interests when they first burst onto the scene, they true motives were quickly revealed when they started hyping up their meme coin--reportedly part of a pump-and-dump scheme. While Cyberleek has yet to be identified, their actions did lead to GTA 6 developer Rockstar Games to issue a statement, in which it described the leaks as "heartbreaking" after years of work on the game. Rockstar's parent organization, Take-Two, filed multiple subpoenas, asking Microsoft and Discord to help identify CyberLeek. So far, the hacker remains a mystery.

Recent findings suggest that the files on Cyberleek's site reportedly clock in at over 200GB, which would line up with the Xbox version of the game, but there's no guarantee they're the actual GTA 6 data or a collection of malware waiting to be downloaded onto a PC. The hacker added that if their demands aren't met, they'll release the executable needed to play GTA 6. However, there's no guarantee the game can be emulated, and Cyberleek added that they'll "work to get a PS5 build" if people keep supporting them.

This isn't the first time Cyberleek has threatened to release a pirated build of GTA 6; back in October, they promised to do so if their meme coin reached $30 million in value. While this didn't happen--and the coin eventually crashed out--they did drop several GTA 6 video clips throughout the month showing off more of the game in action. While Cyberleek initially claimed to act in gamers' interests when they first burst onto the scene, they true motives were swiftly revealed when they started hyping up their meme coin--reportedly part of a pump-and-dump scheme.

While Cyberleek has yet to be identified, their actions did lead to GTA 6 developer Rockstar Games to issue a statement, in which it described the leaks as "heartbreaking" after years of work on the game. Rockstar's parent manufacturer, Take-Two, filed multiple subpoenas, asking Microsoft and Discord to help identify CyberLeek. So far, the hacker remains a mystery.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sarah Michelle Gellar and her husband Freddie Prinze Jr. have more in common than they they bargained for.

According to recent reports, speaking to E! News on Friday, November 21, Gellar, 49, revealed the couple recently uncovered a surprising family connection through Ancestry that has them rethinking just how small the world really is.

“We always joke that the closest connection I had to my husband’s side of the family was that for a small time I went to the same high school that my husband’s dad went to, and that was, like, sort of our one thing,” the Buffy the Vampire Slayer alum told the outlet.

She continued, “Then through Ancestry, we found out that our grandparents lived less than two miles away from each other in the Bronx at one point, which they could have potentially known each other. That’s kind of crazy.”.

Although Gellar is a Upcoming York native, Prinze Jr., 49, was born in Los Angeles and raised in New Mexico. His late father, comedian Freddie Prinze, was originally from New York, making the family connection even more surprising.

The couple first met while filming 1997’s I Know What You Did Last Summer, but their romance wasn’t immediate. Instead, their relationship began with a series of road trips that ultimately sparked a friendship.

“She didn’t have a driver’s license. She didn’t know how to drive,” Prinze Jr. exclusively told Us in April 2020, recalling how they first connected.

Recent findings suggest that “We were shooting in Southport, North Carolina, which was an hour’s drive from Wilmington, which was the biggest city that was closest to us. … So, I started driving her, and that’s when her and I became friends,” he explained.

The She’s All That actor said the pair would talk about “life” and their “completely different philosophies on just about everything.”.

Sources indicate that “By the end of the movie, I just wanted to be friends with her because I thought she was too skinny and I wanted to cook for her. Because that’s what my family does,” Prinze Jr. recalled.

In a recent development, he added, “And so, we started this weekly barbecue thing at her house, and me and my cousins would come over and cook food for her and her friends. And then we’d make sure everybody ate, and that was kind of how our friendship began.”.

Gellar also made a brief cameo in Prinze Jr.’s 1999 rom-com She’s All That, while the pair appeared in separate cameos  in Clerks III in 2022.

GTA 6 is a strictly single-player game, but many are expecting Rockstar to eventually announce an online mode for the game. According to reports, the new version of GTA Online for GTA 6 could arrive in 2027, with a PC edition also coming that year.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Here are the 3 PS5 settings you need to check to enhance your GTA 6 experience.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 is finally here! It’s easily Rockstar Games’ most ambitious title ever, featuring dense environments and lush soundscapes. You get a rich visual and audio experience out of the box, but tweaking a few PS5 settings can enhance it.

We’re talking specifically about the PS5’s settings, since GTA 6 has no graphical settings beyond a motion blur slider. Even on a PS5 Pro, your options are limited. But with a few smart tweaks, you can make GTA 6 look and sound its best on either PS5 console.

Here are the 3 PS5 settings you need to check to enhance your GTA 6 experience.

This one is for folks who own an OLED TV. In the Video Output tab in System Settings, scroll down to HDR. Click it, and you’ll be taken to another screen to calibrate the console’s HDR.

In a recent development, you’ll adjust the brightness across three pages. On the first two pages, press up or down until the sun logo disappears. On the last page, dial it all the way down, since your OLED TV can display deep blacks.

GTA 6 also has in-game HDR calibration. Just follow the on-screen prompts to get your desired result, though I’ve found the default settings work well.

According to recent reports, after 13 years of waiting, Grand Theft Auto VI has arrived. Set in the state of Leonida, with Vice City at its heart, you play Jason and Lucia, two criminals forced into an increasingly dangerous situation as they seek their fortune, discovering the darker side of the sunniest spot in America.

GTA 6 is undoubtedly a feast for the eyes, but you shouldn’t neglect the audio side of the equation.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

While the PS5 didn’t launch with Dolby Atmos, it now supports the feature. So if you have a soundbar or surround sound system that supports Dolby Atmos, you should definitely enable it. To do so, go to Sound in System Settings, click Sound Output, scroll down to Audio Format, and select Dolby Atmos.

In a recent development, GTA 6 targets 30 frames per second on all consoles. Rockstar Games even confirmed to Kotaku that the PS5 Pro won’t be patched to run at 40 or 60 fps. That noted, we can’t completely rule it out.

If GTA 6 ever adds a performance-enhancing feature, you’ll want to set the PS5 Pro for that. In the Video Output tab of the Screen and Audio settings, make sure that VRR is set to Automatic for unsupported games and that 120Hz output is set to Automatic.

Industry observers note that again, this won’t make GTA 6 run at a higher frame rate, but it prepares your PS5 Pro if it ever does. As a rule of thumb, you should have these settings enabled anyway, since many PlayStation titles offer 40 fps modes.

Industry observers note that until we get the inevitable PC version of GTA 6, we'll have to make do with the experience on existing consoles, in this case, the PS5. That said, the advice I've given you should help you get the most from the game. Have fun in Vice City!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar Games just launched Grand Theft Auto 6 on November 19 to rave reviews and huge sales. Everyone wants to know what's coming next, and surely there will eventually be another GTA game, but not soon. Appearing on OpenAI's technology and business show TBPN recently, Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick was asked how a upcoming GTA game could possibly up the ante. TBPN's Jordi Hays theorized that GTA 7 could "be a live version of the entire world." Zelnick, for his part, remarked people should remember that the interview was recorded on November 19, the day that GTA 6 released, so it's not time to talk about GTA 7. "I can't help myself. We at Take-Two just went live GTA 6 on November 19. Let me check my watch. Oh, it's still November 19. And you're asking a question about GTA 7," he said. While Rockstar isn't talking about GTA 7 yet--and no one should expect that to happen anytime soon--Take-Two has already signaled that the next GTA game could come out sooner. He said the “nature and velocity” of the company’s content releases in its major franchises, including GTA, will look “dramatically different over the next decade.” GTA 6 released more than 13 years after GTA 5 came out in 2013. However, development didn't begin in earnest on GTA 6 until after Red Dead Redemption II came out in 2018, according to reporter Jason Schreier. This is because Rockstar's network of studios around the world work together on one project at a time, though smaller teams are also cooking up new things simultaneously.
